title: I. Strange Process
statement:
You are given three arrays:

We perform the following process on these arrays. The process consists of $$m$$ stages. During the $$i$$-th stage, the following occurs:

An array of $$m$$ numbers from $$0$$ to $$n$$ is called achievable if it can be obtained as a result of this process as the array $$b$$.

Your task is to count the number of achievable arrays.

The first line contains two integers $$n$$ and $$m$$ ($$1 $\leq n, m \leq 10^4$$$).

The second line contains $$m$$ integers $$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_m$$ ($$1 $\leq c_i \leq 50$$$).

Print one integer — the number of achievable arrays, taken modulo $$998244353$$.
input: Input The first line contains two integers $$n$$ and $$m$$ ($$1 $\leq n, m \leq 10^4$$$). The second line contains $$m$$ integers $$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_m$$ ($$1 $\leq c_i \leq 50$$$).
output: Output Print one integer — the number of achievable arrays, taken modulo $$998244353$$.
